Title: Product Manager Platform

# About Nscale
Nscale is taking on the hyperscalers by building a vertically integrated GenAI cloud platform.
We own the data centres, software, and applications that power today's AI stack using sustainable technology solutions.
We thrive on a culture of relentless innovation, ownership, and accountability, where every team member takes pride in their work and drives it with excellence and urgency.
As an Nscaler, you'll build trust through openness and transparency, where everyone is inspired to do their best work.
Collaboration is key, and we work together swiftly and respectfully, embracing adaptability and resilience in all we do.
# About the role
Product Managers at Nscale own the definition, delivery, and ongoing evolution of a part of the Nscale cloud platform.
You partner closely with engineering, design, research, and go-to-market teams to translate customer problems and business goals into shippable product outcomes.
PMs work across the full breadth of the Nscale cloud, from core infrastructure primitives to managed platform services, developer experience, and internal tools, wherever product leverage is needed.
As a Senior Product Manager, you operate at team scope.
In this role, you will own a major area of the cloud platform and drive end-to-end projects, from problem framing through launch and iteration, delivered within the EU and tailored to the needs of European customers and regulatory requirements.
Equally central to the role is a deep grounding in cloud and platform technologies, with a particular focus on things such as security, compliance, and cryptography, which sit at the heart of how Nscale earns the trust of European customers.
# What you'll be doing
- Own the strategy and roadmap for a significant part of the cloud platform within your team.
- Lead end-to-end, cross-functional projects across the EU, from problem framing through launch, measurement, and iteration.
- Deliver product outcomes that meet the needs of European customers, including data residency, sovereignty, and regulatory requirements.
- Embed security, compliance, and cryptography into your product area, ensuring platform technologies meet the highest standards.
- Drive meaningful ambiguity: clarify unclear problem statements, align stakeholders, and define what "done" looks like.
- Partner with design and research to shape deep product experiences and validate hypotheses before committing engineering resources.
- Mentor junior product managers and raise the quality bar for PRDs, reviews, and product decisions across the team.
- Represent your product area in planning, reviews, and leadership updates.
- Define and drive the metrics that matter for your area.
# What you need
- 5–8 years of product management experience in software or technology, with a track record of owning significant product areas.
- Strong technical fluency: you can lead discussions with engineering on architecture, trade-offs, and feasibility.
- Strong familiarity with cloud and platform technologies, with a focus on security, compliance, and cryptography.
- Demonstrated ability to move from an ambiguous problem space to shipped product outcomes.
- Experience mentoring or informally leading peers.
- Excellent written and verbal communication; you can make complex product decisions legible to a broad audience.
# Nice to haves
- Degree in computer science, engineering, or a related field, or prior experience as an engineer.
- Experience in cloud infrastructure, developer platforms, enterprise software, or AI/ML products.
- Familiarity with the EU technology landscape, including data residency, sovereignty, and regulatory requirements (e.g. GDPR, EU AI Act).
- Experience operating in high-growth or early-stage environments.
Join Nscale as we build a world-class AI cloud platform.
If you're excited about owning a meaningful product area and raising the bar for the team around you, we'd love to hear from you!
# Equal Opportunities Statement
We strongly encourage applications from people of colour, the LGBTQ+ community, people with disabilities, neurodivergent people, parents, carers, and people from lower socio-economic backgrounds.
If there’s anything we can do to accommodate your specific situation, please let us know.

The employee may be required to perform additional duties, tasks, and responsibilities as assigned by management, consistent with the skills and qualifications required for the role.

> Figma is growing our team of passionate creatives and builders on a mission to make design accessible to all.
> Figma’s platform helps teams bring ideas to life—whether you're brainstorming, creating a prototype, translating designs into code, or iterating with AI.
> From idea to product, Figma empowers teams to streamline workflows, move faster, and work together in real time from anywhere in the world.
> If you're excited to shape the future of design and collaboration, join us!
The Figma Research team is hiring an experienced researcher for our Rapid Research program.
We're product builders who bring research expertise to the team, working closely with designers, product managers, and engineers to clarify problems, test ideas, and recommend what to change—often in one- to two-week sprints.
You'll rotate across product areas, ramp up quickly, and build relationships as you go, energized by unfamiliar products and ambiguous problems and ready to take initiative rather than wait for a fully scoped brief.
You bring strong opinions about what makes a great experience, grounded in the needs of the people using it, spot connections across product areas, and combine deep qualitative and quantitative research expertise with a flexible, resourceful approach to moving quickly without sacrificing rigor.
Beyond individual studies, you bring a clear point of view on what to build or change, tailor your communication to your audience, and are willing to challenge assumptions and say the hard thing with care—asking for help when you need it and offering it when others do.
This is a full time role that can be held from one of our US hubs or remotely in the United States.
# What you'll do at Figma
- Scope and run focused research in quick sprints, using sound methods to answer the questions most likely to change a product decision
- Turn findings into specific recommendations a designer or PM can act on, working through tradeoffs and helping the team put them into practice
- Present product recommendations to cross-functional teams and senior leadership, telling the story behind the data, not just reporting insights
- Rotate across product areas and teams as needed, building credibility and relationships quickly without being embedded long-term
- Contribute beyond research studies by using our products, joining design reviews, and helping teams recognize when they have enough information to act
- Bring clarity to ambiguous problems, challenge assumptions, and adjust the scope or approach as you learn
- Experiment with tools, templates, and workflows to make research faster and sharper
# We'd love to hear from you if you have
- 7+ years of experience in research at high-growth product organizations, UX/design agencies, or strategic consultancies focused on digital experiences
- Proficiency in mixed methods research, including qualitative approaches such as interviews and quantitative approaches such as surveys and data analysis
- Strong product judgment, with examples of specific recommendations you made and how they shaped the product, backed by strong communication and storytelling skills with a track record of securing executive buy-in
- Experience ramping up quickly on new projects and delivering clear recommendations in oneto two-week research sprints, turning ambiguous problems into clear questions and a practical path forward
- A scrappy, flexible approach, adapting to changing priorities and tight timelines while maintaining sound research methods, including active use of AI tools to improve speed, quality, or scale
# While it's not required, it's an added plus if you also have
- Proficiency in designing and prototyping, ideally within the Figma suite of tools
- Familiarity with researching design tools, developer tools, creative software, or other products people use to build things
